item: airplane mode's socket guard is installed whatever OO_NO_SCHEDULER says
key_paths: src/api/main.py; src/api/unlock.py; tests/test_guard_always_installed_r646.py; tests/conftest.py; docs/SECURITY.md; docs/USER_MANUAL.md; CLAUDE.md
summary: OO_NO_SCHEDULER=1 stopped the background scheduler and also left the airplane socket guard out at all three install sites (lifespan, deferred startup, unlock), so an airplane mode engaged later on a headless instance rested on the per-call refusals alone. The guard is now installed whatever that flag says; only OO_AIRPLANE_SOCKET_GUARD=0 leaves it out, and only the boot's kill-switch engage stays gated on OO_NO_SCHEDULER. R644's serving-gate waiver for OO_NO_SCHEDULER=1 is dropped; the test harness opens the gate for in-process clients explicitly. Release line: with the background scheduler turned off (OO_NO_SCHEDULER=1), airplane mode now blocks every outside connection at the socket, as it does in a normal start.
